subject: Next steps — data anchoring & DR options for MediqHealth
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@mediqhealth.com>, procurement@mediqhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps — data anchoring & DR options for MediqHealth

Hi Liam / Procurement team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — helpful conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can validate compliance constraints and narrow to a recommended implementation pattern: 

Call recap (short):
- Primary requirement: anchor PII-derived request logs for EU users within EU geographic boundaries. Mediq wants EU anchoring for storage and ability to prevent cross-border replication unless explicitly allowed.
- DR/Failover: Need a warm-standby failover path in US that can be activated for 1–2 hour outages, but you require written controls on when that happens and a last-resort manual approval path.
- Retention: Default request log retention max 30 days, with ability to configure 90 days for incident investigations. Some data categories require shorter retention (tokens w/ full PHI) — preference is auto-purge at 7 days unless escalated.
- Logging / audit: Must provide immutable audit logs (KMS-protected) and preserve request/response metadata for at least 90 days in EU for compliance, with redaction options for response bodies.

Questions we promised to follow up on:
1) Can Redwood pin both request payloads and derived logs exclusively to an EU region while allowing a US warm-standby for compute only (no automatic data replication)?
2) What are the RTO/RPO bounds for the warm-standby path and how do they change if the standby needs to access logs cross-region under an emergency waiver?
3) What encryption and KMS options do you need so Mediq can manage EU keys (bring-your-own-key)?
4) Editable retention SLA and automated data deletion processes for EEA-subject data (DSAR support).

Proposed short-term next steps:
- I attached a one-pager (Redwood_Data_Controls_Summary.pdf) and a draft SOW skeleton (Draft_SOW_MediqHealth.docx) that map options to costs. Please review the controls page — the bolded section describes our EU-anchoring pattern and the associated opt-in for a manual emergency failover.
- Can you confirm whether procurement wants a hard prohibition on any cross-border replication (i.e., never) or a conditional approach with audit + authorization?
- If OK, let’s schedule a 30-minute tech review with your security/infra team + our infra engineer (Ben) tomorrow or Thursday to go over KMS and audit log examples.

Available slots: Wed 10:00–11:30 & Thu 14:00–16:00 (CEST). I can also shift.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Redwood Inference — Production-first inference runtime for LLMs

Attachments: Redwood_Data_Controls_Summary.pdf (1 page stub), Draft_SOW_MediqHealth.docx (outline)

From: Liam Carter <liam.carter@mediqhealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@mediqhealth.com
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 12:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Next steps — data anchoring & DR options for MediqHealth

Avery — thanks for the recap and the docs. Quick answers from our side: 

- Procurement preference: conditional approach. We cannot accept any routine cross-border replication for EU-production data. An emergency manual waiver (audit + CTO approval) is acceptable, provided we get a clear trail and a time-limited window.
- Retention: Default 30 days is fine for request logs, but any logs that contain direct PHI must be set to 7 days and flagged for immediate purge after investigation.
- KMS: We will require BYOK for the EU key and regional key material to stay in an EU KMS/HSM.

Tech team is available Thurs 15:00–15:30 CEST for a short walkthrough. Please add Ben from your side.

Also — can you confirm whether Redwood can offer redaction-at-ingest (we want to avoid storing full response bodies in logs when a document contains PHI)?

Thanks,
Liam Carter
Head of Platform Security — MediqHealth
liam.carter@mediqhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam Carter <liam.carter@mediqhealth.com>, procurement@mediqhealth.com
Date: Wed, 4 Aug 2027 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — data anchoring & DR options for MediqHealth

Folks — quick technical note ahead of Thurs:

- Pinning model / request artifacts to EU: Redwood supports region pinning at the tenant level. We can enforce that request payloads and derived logs remain in EU storage buckets encrypted with a customer-supplied EU KMS key.
- Warm standby: compute-only warm-standby in another region is supported but we treat it as compute-only — logs are not automatically replicated. Access to EU logs from the standby requires a documented emergency process which we can gate behind a manual approval API call and an audit trail (we produce an immutable event showing who approved and when).
- RTO/RPO: Typical warm-standby RTO is 30–90 minutes depending on workforce orchestration and snapshot freshness; RPO for logs is near-zero if we use cross-region snapshot transfers, but since you want no automatic replication, RPO will depend on whether you allow encrypted snapshot transfer under a waiver. If waiver is allowed, we can document 15–60 min RPO depending on snapshot cadence.
- Redaction-at-ingest: We offer an ingest-time filter pipeline that can redact or hash sensitive fields before persistence. For PHI-heavy content we recommend a two-stage approach: redaction default + secure escrow for redacted payloads only accessible under strict controls.

I will bring a short slide to the call showing KMS flows and the emergency approval API.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Liam Carter <liam.carter@mediqhealth.com>, procurement@mediqhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 16:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — data anchoring & DR options for MediqHealth

Thanks all — quick final notes and concrete asks before the tech session: 

Action items for Mediq before Thurs 15:00 CEST:
- Confirm whether procurement wants the emergency waiver to be (a) time-limited + auto-expire after X hours, and (b) require CTO-level sign-off. If you have a preferred X (we suggested 4 hours default), let us know.
- Share a short list of the top 3 log fields you consider PHI so Ben can tailor the redaction examples.

Action items for Redwood (we will complete before the call):
- Send a one-page KMS flow diagram showing BYOK import + region key material lifecycle (attached: Redwood_Data_Controls_Summary.pdf).
- Prepare a short readout for RTO/RPO delta across options and a cost delta table for EU-only vs EU + manual-waiver warm-standby (we'll include this in the SOW skeleton).
- Provide a sample audit event payload and where it lives (immutable event store with HMAC + KMS envelope).

I attached the one-pager again and the SOW draft; please review and mark any non-starters. Meeting invite sent for Thu 15:00–15:30 CEST.

If procurement confirms the waiver shape (time-limited + CTO approval), we will include language in the SOW and propose a short legal addendum documenting the emergency access process.

Best,
Avery

Attachments: Redwood_Data_Controls_Summary.pdf, Draft_SOW_MediqHealth.docx
